---
title: "The extraction pipeline"
description: "Follow spreadsheet logic, describe the model, and generate a verified Python implementation."
---

An Excel workbook contains more than numbers. Its formulas encode a
computational model: inputs flow through calculations and produce outputs.
The extraction pipeline follows those relationships and makes the model
explicit.

```{mermaid}
flowchart LR
    Workbook["Excel workbook"] --> Model["Computational model"]
    Model --> Guide["User guide from bindings"]
    Model --> Python["Python implementation"]
    Python --> Verify["Differential verification"]
```

This guide develops that story in three steps.

## 1. Follow the spreadsheet logic

Starting from selected outputs, the pipeline follows formula references across
the workbook. Cells become computations and references become dependencies,
forming a computational model of what the spreadsheet does.

[See how extraction works](user-guide/pipeline-overview.qmd)

## 2. Describe how people use the model

Input and output bindings translate workbook coordinates into domain concepts.
They provide the structured foundation for a user guide and show how users
interact with the model without requiring them to understand every cell.

[See how bindings shape the user guide](user-guide/user-guide-bindings.qmd)

## 3. Generate the Python implementation

The graph and bindings become a keyword-only Python API. The generated package
does not require Excel at runtime and can be tested, automated, and integrated
with other software.

[See how the Python implementation works](user-guide/python-implementation.qmd)
